doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Chubby Jackson's bowed bass and Walter Hendl's premiere
summary: A story of the premiere conducted by Walter Hendl in which Chubby Jackson struggled, plus the band's casual time-keeping.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Chubby Jackson was on the band then?

Yes. And I’ve got to tell you this story. We premiered with Walter Hendl, the conductor, pianist and associate conductor with the New York Philharmonic. They still have Stravinsky month at the New York Philharmonic every year. And he had Mickey Fullins playing bass clarinet, which was tom-tom [scats] one strain, and Micky Fullins and Chubby is playing arco, and he doesn’t arco.
He’s not a bow man, right.

Not at all. And he’s going [scats] and Walter Hendl’s going like this, like bring it up. And Chubby got so frustrated and he says, “I already got it up to seven.” He stopped playing. He had to get an amplifier for his bass. He says, “I already got it up to seven” we were on the air. I’ll tell you he couldn’t continue the sound, I mean stunning, with laughter, it’s terrible, terribly unprofessional to be honest with you. But this is the way the band — so say the bus leaves at nine, well people are straggling in at ten, and they were slow at getting to the counter. I mean think about it, you’re on your own trip see? So a lot of © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

musicians that were good, they came to the west coast, when they said it was a nine o’clock call, it means nine o’clock downbeat. You know, you might have forty, fifty men. The clock starts going. So they had to get used to that nine o’clock means nine o’clock at Paramount downbeat. See? A whole different life.
You don’t even think about it.
It must have been a bit of an adjustment.
